facts: ProjectStatus:OK and ServiceReady fire 13ms apart from each other AND before the final workspace-refresh progress notes (spike A cold run: projectStatusOkMs 2293, serviceReadyMs 2306, then statusNotes still show '100% ... Refreshing ...'). Neither signal is proof the index can actually answer a query — both are lies about readiness taken alone.

The gate is therefore a SEMANTIC PROBE, not a status-notification listener: resolve a known symbol from the workspace's own sources and require a non-empty result before opening (INV-READY-2). ServiceReady/ProjectStatus may be used as a hint to START probing, never as the readiness signal itself.

Cold start ranges from 1.5s (warm -data) to a reported 25 minutes on a real monorepo (docs/design/evidence.md) — the gate must be honest rather than fast: a call during warm-up gets isError + progress, never a successful empty or partial result (INV-READY-1), and every waiting call must settle within its deadline even if the workspace never becomes ready (INV-READY-3) — X-001's default deadline value is still an open cross-cutting decision (docs/cross-cutting.md), so make the deadline a parameter, not a hard-coded constant.

java_workspace_status (a separate tool, built later, not part of this feature) exposes this gate's progress as a first-class question an agent can ask — this feature only needs to make that progress state observable/queryable, not build the MCP tool around it.

This gate's probe is also the seam feat-prove-sync uses to demonstrate INV-SYNC-1, before any capability tool exists — expect a dependent feature to call this component's probe function directly, not through MCP.
